_doc: SOURCE-SIDE (axis C) veto list for target_stopwords' content-word rescue: Hebrew/Greek lexemes that are semantically LIGHT — a target word rendering one of these is NOT thereby proven to be a content word, so it must not be rescued out of the stopword list. Computed once, applies to every target language forever (the source inventory is fixed). Without this, LXX-bridge share-pooling wrongly rescues target copulas/quantifiers: spa 'ser' pools to 0.407 across hayah/eimi/ginomai, fra 'tous'/'tout' to 0.966/0.974 across kol/pas. WHY A CURATED LIST: no existing prior-pack column identifies these — measured 2026-08-31, keyness does NOT separate them (hbo:8034 shem 'name' = 0.18 is LOWER than hbo:1961 hayah 'be' = 0.47), word_class tags hayah/eimi as 'content', and pos gives only 'verb'/'noun'. Additive and conservative: adding an entry can only KEEP a word in the stopword list, never remove one. Cross-testament pairs are listed together since the LXX bridge pools them anyway.
_validated: 2026-08-31 against stopwords-iso via evaluate_stopwords' mapping, 36 languages: aggregate precision +0.0135 over the bridge-pooling rule alone; ind +0.079, ben +0.073, hin +0.034, spa -> 1.000. fra/eng/deu held steady, i.e. est/sont/tous/a correctly stayed stopwords.
_narrowed: 2026-08-31: cut from 12 to 7. DROPPED the do/make pair (hbo:6213 asah, grc:4160 poieo) and the say trio (hbo:0559 amar, grc:3004 lego, grc:2036 epo) — those are genuine CONTENT verbs in most targets, and vetoing them wrongly pinned real content words into the stopword list (swe 'göra' to-do/make, fra 'dit' said). The seven kept are unambiguous: copulas, have/there-is, and quantifiers, which are function words in essentially every target. Cases that only LOOKED like the dropped entries working (eng 'what' via amar) were quotation-frame artifacts — right answer, wrong reason.
_extended: 2026-08-31: 7 -> 19. Found systematically, not by eye: for every lexeme the rule rescues on, measure how often the rescued target word is an external (stopwords-iso) stopword across 37 languages; a consistently-high rate means the LEXEME is itself function-class. Verified by inspecting every word each addition newly pins as a stopword — 100% were function words, and no 'face'/'hand'/'one' CONTENT word was affected (those are not frequent-and-dispersed enough to be candidates). Measured +71 true function words at flat-to-better precision (function-class group alone: +0.0012). Deliberately NOT added despite scoring high: hbo:0559 amar 'say', hbo:6213 asah 'do', hbo:5414 natan 'give', hbo:1697 dabar 'word', hbo:3117 yom 'day', hbo:0376 ish 'man', hbo:0935 bo 'come' — these are genuine CONTENT verbs/nouns whose score is inflated by stopwords-iso over-including their target renderings (eng 'say'/'give'/'do', fra 'parole').
